---
title: "GM Session Guide: Chapter 5 (The Wrath of Mars)"
subtitle: "GM guide — Chapter 5"
---

*The crystal-star focus is failing. The party descends past a dead king who has been fighting since 52 BC to a granite altar where a starving god waits. No option at the end saves everyone. That is the point.*

**Level:** 7 (final, no further advancement) · **Players:** 6 (Iris, Julia Jana, Tanit, Rivia, Ursula, Brian) · **Time:** 3-4 hrs · **Type:** Final dungeon crawl + divine confrontation

---

<div class="session-tree">

<details open>
<summary>📋 Session Quick-Reference — The Whole Session in One Page</summary>

| | |
|---|---|
| **Central question** | What do you do with a weapon a god will not stop wanting back? |
| **What must happen** | (1) The party descends from Chapter 4's Core Room, through Vercingetorix's true final stand, to the Antechamber of Mars. (2) The party decides the spear's fate: destroy it, give it to Rome, or give it back to Mars. All three are real endings. |
| **Player goal** | Survive the dungeon, learn the true story from Vercingetorix's Final Death, and choose. |
| **Real stakes** | Whether anyone volunteers to become the vault's new guardian (Destroy). Whether Lucius is trusted enough to take custody (Give to Rome). Whether the party can live with Mars walking away vindicated (Give to Mars). |
| **Session peak moment** | Vercingetorix's Final Death: for one minute, the man behind two centuries of undeath is lucid, and answers three questions truthfully before dissolving to ash. |
| **Closing image** | The crystal-star's light drains out behind the party as they climb. By the time they reach the surface, the marsh is just a marsh again. |

**NPCs active this session:**

| NPC | Location at session start | Wants | Role this session |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tribune Lucius | Travels with the party (only fort NPC who does) | See the spear's fate decided by the party, not by him | Possible guardian in the Destroy ending; takes custody in the Give-to-Rome ending |
| Vercingetorix Bound | Waiting at the Convergence Hall | Fall in a way that finally counts | His true final appearance -- Scene 3, resolved permanently |
| The Session 1 Wight-general | Branch-dependent, Antechamber only | See his three-century oath discharged | One-line cameo, only if spared in Session 1 -- see Scene 4 |

**What is NOT in this session:** the old fort-arena "divine trial" (Mars descending onto Vindolanda's parade ground, three witness-frozen champion trials, Fausta Luperci, Thusnelda). None of that survives in the campaign's actual ending -- see `CAMPAIGN_LOG.md` for why.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🎬 Scene 0: The Crystal Is Failing</summary>

**Read aloud:**

> *The crystal-star's light does not fade when the demon guarding it falls. It gets worse. Cracks spread across its faces like frost across a window, and each one lets out a note too low to be a sound, felt in the teeth more than heard. The floor of the Core Room is warm. Somewhere below, something that has been sleeping under all this weight is starting to notice you.*

> *Tribune Lucius says it before anyone else does. "It's not stopping. Whatever this feeds, it just fed it more than it wanted." He is already moving toward the passage that leads down.*

The crystal cannot be destroyed at the Core Room -- Chapter 4 already established this. Assume the party goes down toward whatever it feeds, rather than leave it burning above a fort full of people.

**Checks:**
- DC 13 Intelligence (Arcana) (passive): the cracking pattern matches the shape of divine attention, not structural failure.
- DC 12 Wisdom (Survival) (active, gauging descent time): the warmth increases at a readable rate. Answer honestly if asked: 3-4 scenes remain before it matters mechanically.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🎬 Scene 1: The Sunken Armory and the Choking Hall</summary>

Load `s5_mars_vault_overview.html`/`.jpg`, zones 2-4.

> *The passage narrows fast. Old weapon racks line a room that has not seen a living hand in longer than the fort has stood. Half the blades have rusted to lace. The other half are untouched, as if the room itself decided which ones still mattered. Beyond it, a hall barely three men wide, walls scored with symbols the torchlight will not sit still on.*

- DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation) (active): the untouched weapons carry a small ram's-eye stamp -- Mars's own mark. One can be taken; counts as a Belatucadrus-grade consecrated weapon for this session only if no other was brought earlier. Using a god's own gift against him is a detail Mars notices and mentions in Scene 4.
- DC 12 Constitution (active, pushing through the Choking Hall): failure deals 1d4 poison damage from the strain. This is a mood beat, not a puzzle.

**Optional encounter:** 2 Shadows or 1 Wraith, reused from earlier sessions, only if the table has burned few resources so far. Read the table, don't force it.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🎬 Scene 2: The Convergence Hall — Three Passages</summary>

Load `s5_mars_vault.html`/`.jpg`, zone 3.

> *The hall opens into three throats of stone, all leading the same direction by different roads. Something about the air says only one of these was meant to be walked.*

| Passage | Contents |
|---|---|
| Left (west) | Pressure-plate rune, DC 14 Perception to spot. Trigger: 3d6 necrotic, 30-ft burst, DC 15 Dexterity half. A dead cultist's journal confirms the two chieftains knew exactly what they served, and did it anyway. |
| Center | 3 Zombies, slow and unsubtle. No trap. The honest road. |
| Right (east) | 1 Specter per party member minus one. No trap, hardest fight of the three. |

No wrong answer, no answer that avoids a cost. Let the party choose based on what they can afford right now, not on which one seems "correct."

</details>

<details>
<summary>🎬 Scene 3: Vercingetorix's Last Stand</summary>

> *He stands where the three passages become one, and for the first time since the fort's gate, you see him clearly. The wounds from that night never closed. They never will. His armor is Gallic work two centuries out of fashion, rusted through in places where a living man would already be dead of infection ten times over. He is not breathing. He was never going to stop being here.*

> *"Again," he says, in Latin thick with an accent that predates the Empire itself. "Always again. Tell me this time is the one that ends it."*

This is his true and final appearance. Use **Vercingetorix Bound** (`npcs/vercingetorix_bound.json`, CR 11): AC 18, HP 150, Multiattack (2, Sword of the Last Charge, 2d6+5 slashing plus 2d8 necrotic), Fear Aura (recharge 5-6, DC 15 Wisdom or Frightened 1 minute), Aura of the Unfinished War (undead allies within 30 ft gain +4 melee damage), Command the Fallen (1/day, raises 1d4 Zombies/Skeletons -- use once, below half HP, not as an opener), Relentless (1/day, drops to 1 HP instead of 0 unless the damage is radiant or from a Belatucadrus-consecrated weapon), Legendary Resistance (1/day), Parry (reaction, +4 AC).

If Relentless triggers, say so plainly: "He should be dead. He isn't. Not yet." This has never been a clean fight for him either.

**Final Death.** When a killing blow lands that Relentless does not prevent:

> *He drops to one knee, not to the ground. For the first time, his eyes focus on something that is actually in front of him instead of some other, older battlefield. "...Ended," he says, like the word is unfamiliar in his own mouth.*

For one minute, his spirit remains, lucid, and answers up to three questions truthfully before dissolving to ash. Hand this over as a gift, not a quiz: Alesia and Caesar's true corruption, why Mars wants the spear (starvation, not conquest), what Vercingetorix actually is (a soldier who was never allowed to stop). He does not know about Corvinus, Brutus, or Pompey -- only his own war. This is the party's first real confirmation of the whole story.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🎬 Scene 4: The Antechamber of Mars</summary>

Load `s5_mars_confrontation.html`/`.jpg`.

> *The passage opens into a circle wide enough to lose an army in. Twelve stones stand at its edge like an audience that arrived centuries early. At the center, a granite altar, chained to the floor by links thick as a man's arm, all of them scored and stretched as if something enormous has strained against them for a very long time. The air itself is red at the edges of your vision, and it is getting redder.*

**Rounds 1-2, presence only.** Radiating cracks pulse (DC 12 Dexterity or 1d6 necrotic crossing one). Legendary Actions still available: Strike (one attack at full bonus), Summon Fallen (a Wraith or Wight, twice at most here).

**The Session 1 Wight-general's cameo (branch on what actually happened):** if he was spared in Session 1, his spirit rises from a plinth, once: *"I held this three hundred years so it would not have to end like this. I am glad I do not have to decide."* Released the moment the spear's fate is settled. If he was destroyed in Session 1, this beat does not happen -- do not manufacture a substitute.

**Round 3+, full manifestation.** Use the existing **Mars** stat block (`npcs/mars.json`, CR 20): AC 22, HP 300, Multiattack (4 Divine Pilum, +12 to hit, range 60 ft, 2d8+7 piercing plus divine), Legendary Resistance (3/day), War Cry (recharge 5-6, DC 18 Wisdom or Frightened 1 minute), Divine Smite (1/round, +4d8 radiant), Legendary Actions (3/round: Strike, God's Eye, Summon Fallen -- max 3 total).

> *"MORTALS," he says, and the word is not loud, only total. "You have carried my anchor through two ghosts and a king who would not die. Now choose, and choose knowing I will remember which one you make."*

</details>

<details>
<summary>⚖️ Decision Point: The Three Horrible Options</summary>

The campaign's actual thesis. Present all three plainly -- none is secretly correct.

| Option | Requires | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Destroy it completely** | Unmaking ritual at the granite altar. Mars opposes with everything he has -- guaranteed full manifestation, fought to the end. | Someone becomes the vault's new guardian, permanently: a PC (ask the player, don't narrate their feelings for them) or Tribune Lucius, if trusted. No volunteer = the ritual fails partway; choose one of the other two. |
| **2. Give it to Rome** | Tribune Lucius takes the spear into official custody, per his orders since Chapter 2. Mars considers this theft -- a shorter, angrier fight (roughly HP 150 or a demonstrated costly tactic). | The crisis ends today. Someday, in a province nobody at this table will ever see, this happens again to somebody else's ancestors. |
| **3. Give it back to Mars** | Return the spear to the altar and step back. No unmaking, no theft, no fight beyond whatever's already been survived. | No one bleeds today. A god who has been right about the nature of war his entire existence walks away vindicated, free to do this again. |

Ask each player what their character actually wants. Let the disagreement between characters be part of the scene. If a corruption-level-5 PC exists, Mars addresses them directly, by name, before anyone else answers -- their honest answer should carry real weight in how the scene closes.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🏛️ Epilogue and DM Notes</summary>

Return to Fort Vindolanda. Corvinus, Cassia, and Varro (who stayed behind per Chapter 4) greet the party, along with Lucius if he didn't stay behind as the Destroy ending's guardian. See `chapter5.qmd` for the full per-ending NPC epilogue table and the citizenship resolution.

**Consistency guard:** Mars is genuinely Mars -- diminished, corrupted, starved by two centuries of the Pax Romana, not an impostor wearing his face. If a player asks "is this really him," any NPC suspicion (Cassia is the natural one) stays suspicion, never confirmation. Do not resolve into "it was someone else all along" -- that idea was considered and explicitly rejected during this campaign's design.

**Commendationes:** one final opportunity -- any character who endures the full dungeon and is present for the ending earns one, filed by Cassia as religious witness. See `chapter5.qmd`'s DM Notes for the full tally guidance.

</details>

</div>
